headline: Nasdaq-100: hawkish front-end repricing meets a closed market, leaving tail risk at the low-band floor into the reopen
body:
This assessment falls inside the weekend CME halt, so no live NQ price path exists and no mean-reversion failure can be developing. The anchor is Friday's completed session, re-verified against the Nasdaq-100 quote page this hour: the index opened 29,545.90, reached 29,752.78, fell to 29,383.92 and closed 29,433.43, down 0.70% from a 29,641.60 previous close. The close sits about 50 points off the low of a 369-point range, a downside reversal inside a finished session. VIX closed 14.43 within a 14.13-14.84 range and carried no volatility premium into the weekend.

The macro driver is a hawkish repricing rather than a price-path event. The Federal Reserve's published Jackson Hole keynote by Chairman Warsh states that policymakers must be confident underlying inflation is moving to target "clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do." Reuters reporting confirms the market response: the 2-year yield rose 11 basis points to 4.34%, its highest in a month, the 10-year rose to 4.72% and the 30-year to 5.206%, while CME-implied odds of a September rate increase moved from about 35% to about 60%. The H.15 release shows official constant-maturity yields through 27 August at 4.20% for the 2-year and 4.67% for the 10-year, so the repricing sits at the front end.

Cross-asset evidence conflicts rather than aligns. The latest session left the semiconductor complex broadly lower, with NVDA down 4.57% and ARM down 6.33%, while the megacap tape was split, with AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL and META higher. Under the risk definitions in force, conflicting internals raise Stress and reduce directional conviction; they are not an amplifier of the pathological price path Tail measures. WTI at 83.44 dollars ended last week about 4% lower, with verified weekend reporting describing Strait of Hormuz traffic as still below normal under a sanctions and blockade regime rather than a fresh supply discontinuity.

None of the amplifiers that would justify a higher Tail are present: there is no observed persistent directional efficiency, no shallow-pullback sequence, no repeated extension after failed retracements, and no market in which any of those could be forming. Tail therefore rests at the low-band floor of 5 and the mapped policy state is EA_ON. Stress at 30 reflects the untested front-end repricing meeting a data-heavy week: ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on Tuesday, ADP and the Broadcom report on Wednesday, ISM Services on Thursday and August payrolls on Friday. One narrow observation window is flagged across the 22:00-23:30 UTC Sunday reopen, where that repricing first meets thin liquidity and two-way gap risk. Monday 31 August is also month-end, and the UK summer bank holiday leaves London closed, thinning European depth. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, covering the weekend halt from Saturday evening through the hour before this one. The series was uniformly green with Tail fixed at 5, dominant mode normal, and Stress confined to a 25-29 band that drifted up only in the final hours. Confidence decayed from 66 to 58 through the overnight hours as published evidence aged across the closed market, then recovered through 64, 72 and 80 to 85 as primary sources were re-verified on each hourly refresh. No hour in the window contained an observable NQ price path.
outlookSummary: The next three projected hours remain inside the weekend CME halt, where no price path can form; Tail stays at the low-band floor of 5 while Stress drifts from 30 to 31 and Confidence eases from 86 to 84. From the projected 22:00 UTC reopen the conditional Tail lifts to 12, still inside the low band and far below the block threshold, covering the first live test of Friday's front-end repricing. It then eases through 11 and 10 across the Asian session to an overnight low of 8, lifts through 9 and 10 into a continental-only European morning thinned by the UK bank holiday, and reaches a projected peak of 15 across the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open, where opening-auction imbalance meets month-end rebalancing on the final session of August. The window closes at 13 as month-end market-on-close flow builds into the U.S. afternoon. Every projected hour maps to EA_ON and green; Stress peaks at 34 in the moderate band and Confidence decays to 70 at the far end of the projection.
